To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
South Africa could save R2.2 billion per year by using newer, cheaper, safer drugs for first line treatment of HIV.

the use of newer, safer, cheaper antiretrovials in first-line therapy for HIV can significantly reduce the costs of antiretrovial therapy in South Africa, and that this can be done without compromising the quality of care.
newer, cheaper, safer antiretrovirals may become available in the next few years and that these drugs could save South Africa billions of rand.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential cost savings to the national HIV treatment programme of newer, safer antiretrovals, which may be available in the near future.
the cost-effectiveness of newer drugs in HIV, with the goal of reducing costs and improving health outcomes.
the cost-effectiveness and cost-saving potential of new drug development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the South African government has to date not been able to justify the cost of the antiretrovirus drugs it has purchased for the HIV programme.
newer antiretrovirus regimens may have the potential to reduce the cost of antiretrovial therapy, but only if they are proven in the appropriate trials.
the cost of ART is not a barrier to universal coverage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are in a position to save money by switching to new regimens, but this requires careful consideration and a willingness to change.
we have shown that newer drugs, if they are safe and effective, could reduce the cost of antiretrovials by 30–40%.
newer antiretrovials are likely to be more efficacious than current first-line regimens, but the cost savings are only likely to be realised if the trials are conducted in a cost-effective manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current first-line regimen is not the best we can offer.
the current first-line regimens may no longer be the best value for money.
we need to ensure that these trials are done, and that the results are implemented in the South African HIV programmes as soon as possible.
